title: The sharp cubic Legendre floor is uniform on controlled bounded seed families

seed_family.definition: S(B,u_0,u_1) consists of symmetric centered unit-variance laws with |X|<=B and u=-kappa_4(X) in [u_0,u_1], where 0<u_0<=u_1<=2.
seed_family.compactness: Uniform support and moment constraints make the family weakly compact; Gaussian interpolation is smooth for t<1.
seed_family.uniform_remainder: The K1687 Hermite expansion and its q-derivative have O_(B,u_0)(q^(7/2)) and O_(B,u_0)(q^(5/2)) remainders uniformly on the family.

global_branch.coercive_bound: Cauchy gives j_X(q)>=q^2/E[H_3(Y_t)^2]>=q^2/C_B, with C_B finite uniformly from |X|<=B.
global_branch.consequence: For one r_0(B,u_0)>0 every global minimizer of j_X(q)-rq lies on the uniform small-q branch.

legendre.sharpness: If S(B,u_0,u_1) contains X_*, the K1702 seed attains the cubic coefficient 27/4.

scope_guard: The support ceiling B and defect floor u_0 are load-bearing. Seeds with B growing or u tending to zero with coupling, exact finite-strength optimization and non-product field laws remain open.
